open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\) that every exact transformed-KDE leading score differs from its frozen-coefficient, frozen-pole response by \(o(\sqrt{L_n})\) in cellwise \(L^2\), and prove a uniform \(O(1)\) bound for the order-minus-two score.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen assumptions and established nested derivative determine the local intensities and angular constant, but no established node supplies the variable-coefficient transformed-kernel parametrix estimate. The orchestrator expressly requires oeq:uniform-critical-control to remain open until that estimate is derived.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the four mass-change identities, the exact anisotropic angular integral, all four independent-cell weights, the absence of off-grid logarithmic blocks, and a covariance perturbation inequality reducing the remaining claim to the missing score estimates.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal F_s\), a grid point \(y=y_j\), and put \(x=R_0(y)\).  The three population change-of-variables equations are
\[
 f_{C1}(p(x))\det S(x)=f_{C0}(x),\qquad
 q(T(y))\det H(y)=f_{T1}(y),\qquad
 q(p(x))\det S(x)=f_{T0}(x).
\]
Because \(T(y)=p(x)\) and \(D(y)=S(x)^{-1}H(y)\), these equations and the definition of \(\alpha\) imply
\[
 f_{C0}(x)\det D(y)
 =f_{C1}(T(y))\det H(y)
 =\frac{f_{T1}(y)}{\alpha(y)},
 \qquad
 f_{T0}(x)\det D(y)=f_{T1}(y).
\tag{1}
\]
In the order-minus-one part of def:nested-derivative, the two control noises have multiplier \(\alpha(y)\), whereas the two treated noises have multipliers of absolute value one.  Squaring those multipliers and using (1) shows that their respective local source intensities in treated-post coordinates are
\[
 \alpha(y)f_{T1}(y),\quad \alpha(y)f_{T1}(y),\quad
 f_{T1}(y),\quad f_{T1}(y).
\tag{2}
\]
For a constant positive-definite matrix \(B_0\), the gradient of the fundamental solution of \(-\operatorname{div}(B_0\nabla\cdot)\) is
\[
 \nabla\Gamma_{B_0}(z)
 =-\frac{B_0^{-1}z}
 {2\pi\sqrt{\det B_0}\,z^{\mathsf T}B_0^{-1}z}.
\]
With \(z=B_0^{1/2}r\omega\), \(\omega\in\mathbb S^1\), and
\(\int_{\mathbb S^1}\omega\omega^{\mathsf T}\,d\omega=\pi I_2\), direct integration gives
\[
 \int_{c h<\lVert B_0^{-1/2}z\rVert<c_0}
 \nabla\Gamma_{B_0}(z)\nabla\Gamma_{B_0}(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz
 =\frac{B_0^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_0}}\log(1/h)+O(1).
\tag{3}
\]
Thus (2), independence in ass:four-sample-design, and the cell-ratio weights give the diagonal block
\[
 \left\{\alpha(y)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})
 +\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\right\}
 f_{T1}(y)\frac{B(y)^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B(y)}}.
\]
Since \(B(y)=f_{T1}(y)H(y)^{-1}\), this is exactly
\[
 \frac{\left\{\alpha(y)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})
 +\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\right\}
 \sqrt{\det H(y)}H(y)}{4\pi f_{T1}(y)}=V_j.
\tag{4}
\]
For \(j\ne k\), injectivity of \(R_0\) and \(T\), together with ass:fixed-separated-grid and uniform ellipticity, keeps the two cellwise poles a fixed positive distance apart.  The product of their two order-minus-one singularities is integrable on \(\mathbb T^2\), so it contributes \(O(1)\), rather than a logarithm, to the cross block.  The bounded \(L^2\) harmonic score in thm:nested-derivative similarly has variance \(O(1)\) and, by Cauchy--Schwarz, covariance \(O(\sqrt{L_n})\) with a leading score of norm \(O(\sqrt{L_n})\).

Consequently, the claimed covariance follows once one proves, uniformly in \(P\), that each exact transformed-KDE leading score differs in \(L^2(P_g)\) from its frozen-pole counterpart by \(o(\sqrt{L_n})\), and that the order-minus-two term in def:nested-derivative has \(O(1)\) score norm.  Indeed, if \(U_{g,h}\) is a leading score, \(U^0_{g,h}\) its frozen-pole version, and \(R_{g,h}\) contains the order-minus-two and harmonic terms, then
\[
 \frac{1}{L_n}\left\lVert
 \operatorname{Cov}(U_{g,h_n}+R_{g,h_n})
 -\operatorname{Cov}(U^0_{g,h_n})\right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq
 \frac{\lVert U_{g,h_n}-U^0_{g,h_n}\rVert_2
       (\lVert U_{g,h_n}\rVert_2+\lVert U^0_{g,h_n}\rVert_2)}{L_n}
 +O(L_n^{-1/2}),
\]
which is \(o(1)\) under precisely those two estimates.  Equations (1)--(4) therefore determine the only possible logarithmic limit, but the frozen core does not contain the uniform transformed-kernel parametrix estimate needed to complete the operator-norm convergence.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Establish the uniform oracle-to-plug-in expansion with remainder \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\), including generated-target, coefficient, moving-pole, and selected-lift effects.
open_obligations.obstruction: The oracle triangular array satisfies Lindeberg and the deterministic bias is negligible, but Frechet differentiability along fixed smooth paths does not control shrinking-bandwidth empirical directions. The required tame nonlinear estimate is an unresolved part of oeq:uniform-critical-control.
open_obligations.attempted: Completed the oracle envelope, Lindeberg, covariance, cell-ratio, and bias reductions and isolated the exact uniform stochastic expansion still required.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let
\[
 S_n=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac1{n_g}
       \sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i}).
\]
The four cell samples are independent by ass:four-sample-design.  A kernel-smoothed order-minus-one Green response has envelope \(O(h_n^{-1})\).  Since \(n_g\geq n\), every summand of \(\sqrt{n/L_n}S_n\) is bounded in norm by
\[
 \frac{C}{\sqrt{nL_n}\,h_n}=o(1),
\tag{5}
\]
because \(n h_n^2L_n\to\infty\) under ass:polynomial-bandwidth.  Hence the triangular-array Lindeberg sum is eventually zero for every fixed truncation threshold.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_P\!\left(\sqrt{n/L_n}S_n\right)
 =\frac1{L_n}\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac n{n_g}
   \operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi_{g,h_n}(X)).
\tag{6}
\]
Thus ass:cell-ratios and the asserted covariance convergence in lem:full-critical-covariance would give convergence of this matrix to \(V(P)\).  The Cram\'er--Wold argument applied to (5) would then yield the Gaussian limit for the oracle linear term.

The deterministic smoothing bias is \(O(h_n^{s-2})\), and lem:bandwidth-feasibility gives
\[
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\,h_n^{s-2}\longrightarrow0.
\]
It remains necessary to establish the uniform stochastic expansion
\[
 \widehat\tau-\tau(P)=S_n+b_n+r_n,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\sqrt{n/L_n}\,\lVert b_n\rVert\to0,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \mathbb P_P\!\left(\sqrt{n/L_n}\,\lVert r_n\rVert>\epsilon\right)\to0
\tag{6}
\]
for every \(\epsilon>0\), including the random coefficient, generated-target, moving-pole, and selected-lift effects.  Neither Frechet differentiability at a fixed smooth path nor the bandwidth arithmetic alone proves (6) for shrinking-bandwidth empirical directions.  The unresolved tame estimate in oeq:uniform-critical-control is exactly the missing implication.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove normalized \(L^2\) stability and a uniform fourth-moment envelope for every cross-fitted adjoint score under estimated coefficients, pullbacks, harmonic scores, and moving poles.
open_obligations.obstruction: Cross-fitting gives conditional independence but does not control translation of a mollified \(1/r\) singularity. The frozen core supplies neither the necessary pilot pole rate nor the critical-scale transformed-kernel stability bound.
open_obligations.attempted: Proved that the displayed \(L^2\) stability and fourth-moment bounds imply empirical covariance consistency at rate \(O_{\mathbb P}((\sqrt n h_nL_n)^{-1})\); also derived the uniform eigenvalue lower bound, ridge negligibility, inverse consistency, and exact conditional Gaussian multiplier law.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Write \(\widehat\Psi_{g,i}=\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r(i))}(X_{g,i})\) and \(\Psi_{g,i}=\Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i})\).  Conditional on the opposite-fold pilots, observations in an evaluation fold are independent of the functions used to compute their scores.  Suppose the still-unproved singular-score estimates were available in the quantitative form
\[
 \max_{g,r}\left\lVert
 \widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}
 \right\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}=o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n}),
\tag{7}
\]
and, on pilot events of probability tending to one uniformly,
\[
 \max_{g,r}\mathbb E_{P_g}\!\left[
 \left\lVert\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X)\right\rVert^4
 +\left\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}(X)\right\rVert^4
 \right]=O(h_n^{-2}).
\tag{8}
\]
The order-minus-one Green envelope and its annular integral also give
\(\lVert\Psi_{g,h_n}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}=O(\sqrt{L_n})\).  By Cauchy--Schwarz, (7) then implies
\[
 \frac1{L_n}\left\lVert
 \operatorname{Cov}_{P_g}(\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X))
 -\operatorname{Cov}_{P_g}(\Psi_{g,h_n}(X))
 \right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{9}
\]
Conditional Chebyshev applied entrywise to the fixed-dimensional empirical outer products, using (8), yields an error
\[
 O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\frac1{\sqrt n\,h_nL_n}\right)=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\tag{10}
\]
because \(n h_n^2L_n^2\to\infty\).  Foldwise empirical centering changes neither (9) nor (10).  After multiplication by the displayed factors \(n/n_g\), (9)--(10) prove
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}-\Sigma_{h_n}(P)=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{11}
\]
Combining (11) with lem:full-critical-covariance would prove covariance consistency.

The remaining conclusions would then be algebraic.  Since \(\theta_n=n^{-1}\),
\[
 \left\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^R-V(P)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \left\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}-V(P)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}+n^{-1}.
\]
Furthermore, ass:density-positivity, ass:outer-ellipticity, and \(\rho_{T1}\leq\bar\rho\) imply the uniform block bound
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(V_j(P))
 \geq \frac{\lambda^2}{4\pi C\bar\rho}>0.
\tag{12}
\]
The resolvent identity and (12) therefore give uniform convergence of every ridged block inverse.  Finally, Gaussian multiplier independence gives the exact finite-sample identity
\[
 Z^\star\mid\{X_{g,i}\}\sim N(0,\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}).
\]
The unresolved content is (7)--(8) for adjoint scores computed with estimated coordinate pullbacks, elliptic coefficients, harmonic scores, and moving poles.  Cross-fitting supplies the conditional independence used above but does not itself prove those singular-score estimates.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Transfer the unresolved joint critical CLT and adjoint covariance consistency to the studentized estimation-error and multiplier maxima.
open_obligations.obstruction: Finite-sample ridge invertibility and the multiplier law are exact, but asymptotic coverage cannot be asserted while both parent convergence results remain unproved.
open_obligations.attempted: Completed totalization, conditional Gaussian calibration, the parameter-free limiting maximum distribution, its explicit quantile, and the final uniform quantile-continuity reduction.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The matrix \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}\) is positive semidefinite because it is a nonnegative weighted sum of outer products.  Since \(\theta_n=n^{-1}>0\),
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^R
 =\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}+\theta_nI_{2J}\succ0
\]
in every sample.  Every principal block is therefore invertible, and the maximum in the definition of \(\widehat c_{1-\gamma}\) is a finite nonnegative random variable, so its conditional quantile exists.  Direct calculation using independence and unit variance of the multipliers gives
\[
 Z^\star\mid\{X_{g,i}\}\sim N(0,\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}).
\tag{13}
\]
If thm:joint-critical-clt and thm:adjoint-covariance were established, (13), covariance continuity of finite-dimensional Gaussian laws, and the block inverse conclusion of thm:adjoint-covariance would imply conditional convergence of the multiplier maximum to
\[
 M_P=\max_{1\leq j\leq J}Z_j^{\mathsf T}V_j(P)^{-1}Z_j,
 \qquad Z\sim N(0,V(P)).
\]
Because \(V(P)\) is block diagonal and every block is positive definite, its standardized blocks are independent \(N(0,I_2)\) vectors.  Hence
\[
 \mathbb P(M_P\leq x)=(1-e^{-x/2})^J,qquad x\geq0,
\tag{14}
\]
which is continuous, strictly increasing on \((0,\infty)\), and independent of \(P\).  Its \((1-\gamma)\)-quantile is
\[
 c_{1-\gamma}=-2\log\!\left(1-(1-\gamma)^{1/J}\right).
\]
The same two parent results and Slutsky's theorem would give (14) for the studentized estimation-error maximum.  Uniform conditional quantile convergence would then prove
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\!\left\{
 \tau_j(P)\in\mathcal E_j\text{ for every }1\leq j\leq J
 \right\}\longrightarrow1-\gamma.
\]
Thus finite-sample totalization and the calibration step are complete; the only unclosed part is inheritance of the two parent limits, which themselves require oeq:uniform-critical-control.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the class-uniform upper second-moment bound, including integrated tails for the nonlinear remainder and clipping or lift-branch exceptional events.
open_obligations.obstruction: The fixed-center two-point lower bound is complete, but weak convergence does not imply uniform integrability. No established node controls the exceptional-event contribution at order \(o(L_n/n)\).
open_obligations.attempted: Completed the Hellinger-local two-point lower bound and showed algebraically that the bandwidth window makes the proposed tame-remainder moment bound negligible; isolated the exact exceptional-event probability and integrated-tail estimates required for the upper bound.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let
\[
 \Delta_n=\left|\upsilon^{\mathsf T}
 \{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right|,
 \qquad
 Q_{n,\sigma}=\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}P_{n,\sigma,g}^{\otimes n_g}.
\]
For any estimator, use its projection on \(\upsilon\) in the first block to test the sign by choosing the nearer of the two scalar parameter values.  A testing error under sign \(\sigma\) implies scalar estimation error at least \(\Delta_n/2\); the vector error is no smaller than that scalar error.  The elementary two-point testing identity therefore gives
\[
 \max_{\sigma\in\{+,-\}}
 \mathbb E_{P_{n,\sigma}}
 \left\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P_{n,\sigma})\right\rVert^2
 \geq \frac{\Delta_n^2}{8}
 \left\{1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_{n,+},Q_{n,-})\right\}.
\tag{15}
\]
Choose the amplitude in lem:green-local-alternatives small enough that its product-Hellinger bound makes the braces in (15) at least a fixed positive constant.  The same lemma gives
\[
 \Delta_n^2\geq c(P_0)\zeta^2
 \frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}n,
 \qquad
 \log(1/\varepsilon_n)=\eta\log n=\frac{\eta}{a_h}L_n.
\]
Both alternatives belong to \(\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa(P_0))\).  Taking the infimum over estimators in (15), multiplying by \(n/L_n\), and taking the lower limit proves the claimed fixed-center lower bound with some \(c_0(P_0)>0\).

For the upper bound, the oracle linear term has second moment \(O(L_n/n)\), and lem:bandwidth-feasibility makes the squared deterministic bias \(O(h_n^{2(s-2)})=O(L_n/n)\).  A uniform tame expansion would reduce the remaining moment calculation to
\[
 \mathbb E_P\lVert r_n\rVert^2
 \lesssim
 \left\{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{9/2}}+h_n^{2s-5/2}\right\}^2
 +\mathbb P_P(\text{clipping or lift-branch failure}).
\tag{16}
\]
The polynomial window implies that the first term in (16) is \(o(L_n/n)\): its stochastic ratio is \(O(\log n/(n h_n^9))=o(1)\), and its bias and mixed ratios vanish at \(a_h\geq1/[2(s-2)]\) with \(s\geq8\).  Therefore the asserted upper risk rate would follow from a uniform integrated-tail version of the tame remainder and a bound
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \mathbb P_P(\text{clipping or lift-branch failure})=o(L_n/n).
\]
Those moment and exceptional-event estimates are not consequences of weak convergence and are not present in the frozen core.  The lower bound is complete, but this missing uniform-integrability step prevents a proof of the conjunction stated in thm:matched-critical-risk.
